# ldapium

> ldapium is an OpenLDAP distribution with a web console. The console's JSON HTTP API (under /api) can be driven by scripts and AI agents. This file is an index; the authoritative contract is the OpenAPI 3.1 document.

- OpenAPI spec (machine-readable, always matches the running build): /api/v1/openapi.json
- Server/API discovery (public): /api/v1/meta
- Human-readable API page: /api-docs
- Longer guide with curl examples: docs/api.md in the repository

## Authentication

- A signed session cookie named `ldapium_session` is the only credential. There are no API tokens, no OAuth client credentials and no CORS headers.
- LDAP mode (GET /api/v1/meta -> authMode "ldap"): POST /api/login with {"identity","password"} using a cookie jar, then reuse the jar. Failed logins are rate-limited per IP (429 + Retry-After).
- SSO mode (authMode "sso"): login is a browser OIDC flow; scripted login is not possible.
- Directory operations run as the logged-in identity (LDAP mode) or the configured service account (SSO mode), under that identity's LDAP ACLs. 403 usually means the ACL denies it.

## Endpoint groups

- Discovery (public): /api/v1/meta, /api/v1/openapi.json, /api/auth/config, /api/health/ldap
- Auth: /api/login, /api/logout, /api/me, /api/sso/start, /api/sso/callback
- Server: /api/server-settings, /api/monitor, /api/audit/actions
- Directory: /api/tree, /api/entry, /api/entry/move, /api/password-policies
- Users: /api/users (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE), /api/users/password, /api/users/lock, /api/users/unlock
- Groups: /api/groups (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE), /api/groups/members (POST/DELETE)
- Application profiles (profile admins only; 404 when disabled): /api/v1/applications/...
- Backups (backup admins only; 404 when disabled): /api/v1/backups/...

In the OpenAPI document, `security: []` means public, operations with `x-admin: true` need an administrator DN, everything else needs a session.

## Conventions

- Every error (4xx/5xx, including unknown paths and wrong methods) is one JSON body: {"error", "message", "code", "requestId", "retryable"}. `error` and `message` carry the same text (`message` is a deprecated alias), `code` is a stable snake_case name from a closed, append-only table (see the Error schema and docs/api.md) - branch on `code`, not on the text. `requestId` equals the X-Request-Id response header and the server log line holding the cause. 5xx text is fixed and never carries internal detail; 4xx text never carries a DN. 429 and retryable 503 responses include Retry-After. Exceptions: GET /api/health/ldap ({"reachable": bool}), redirects, and bodiless responses (OPTIONS 204, HEAD).
- HEAD mirrors GET (with an empty body) on every route that has a GET handler, and OPTIONS on routed /api paths returns 204 with an Allow header.
- Writes to application profiles, integration methods and backups are conditional: read the resource, take the ETag response header, send it as If-Match (quoted integer revision; "0" creates). Missing If-Match is 428, stale is 412. Keycloak role operations use the quoted 64-hex fingerprint ETag instead.
- Those same write endpoints also require an `Origin` header equal to the server's own origin and `Content-Type: application/json` (403 / 415 otherwise).
- GET /api/users and /api/groups return at most 5000 entries; `truncated: true` means more exist and there is no cursor yet.
- GET /api/audit/actions pages with `limit` (1-200, default 50) and `before` (use `nextBefore` while `hasMore` is true).
- Backup runs are asynchronous without job IDs: POST /api/v1/backups/jobs/{kind} returns 202; poll GET /api/v1/backups.

## Safety

- `userPassword` is never returned by any endpoint, even hashed.
- POST /api/users/password without `password` returns a server-generated `generatedPassword` once; treat it as a secret and never log it.
- Destructive operations (DELETE users/groups/profiles/connections, entry move, Keycloak role operations, backup runs) are not reversible. Confirm intent before calling them and do not retry blindly.
- Never assume a truncated list is complete. Prefer read-only calls unless the task requires a change.
